title: An Inner Disk in the Large Gap of the Transition Disk SR 24S
question: Does the multiwavelength (0.45, 1.3, 2.75 mm) dust continuum structure of the SR 24S transition disk, including an inner disk, reveal the origin of its large cavity?

data.bands: Band 3 (2.75 mm), plus earlier Band 6 and Band 9

what.value: Band 6 and Band 9 visibilities and calibration

evidence.quote: are explained in (cite: marel2015) and (cite: pinilla2017)

what.value: Total flux at 1.3 mm of 220 mJy

evidence.loc: 3.2 Disk dust mass and spectral index
evidence.quote: Using the total flux at 1.3 mm of 220 mJy (cite: pinilla2017)

evidence.loc: 4.2 Origin of the large gap and ring-like structure
evidence.quote: the accretion rate of $\sim3\times10^{-8}$ $M_{\odot}$  year$^{-1}$ (cite: natta2006)

recipe.method: Gaussian fit with uvmodelfit; phase centre corrected with fixvis
clean with natural weighting; deprojected azimuthally averaged radial profiles

recipe.goal: Optical depth, dust mass and spectral index
recipe.method: optically thin dust mass from flux; tau from brightness temperature; spectral index from 1.3 and 2.75 mm fluxes
fit the real part of the visibilities with 3 models (asymmetric Gaussian ring; plus point source; plus central Gaussian) at each of three bands
key_parameters: 200 walkers, 2000 steps, uniform priors (r_peak 10-80 au, sigma 1-50 au, A 0-1, sigma_inner 0.1-10 au, F_total 0-3 Jy)

recipe.method: qualitative comparison of normalized intensity profiles with planet and dead-zone dust evolution models convolved with an 11 au beam
assumptions: Mie opacities with Ricci et al. 2010 optical constants; temperature power law index -1/2

answer_key.quantity: Band 3 total flux density from image

evidence.quote: The total flux density and the peak brightness from the image is 28.9 mJy

evidence.loc: 3.2 Disk dust mass and spectral index
3.3 Fit of the dust morphology in the visibility plane

answer_key.quantity: Band 3 inner disk flux in 75 mas aperture

evidence.loc: 3.1 Dust morphology and comparison with previous ALMA observations
evidence.quote: with a maximum value of $\tau$ at the peak of emission of 0.37
